Answer quality depends on documentation quality
name: Glean
pros: Genuinely useful for organizations with fragmented knowledge
Respects existing permissions from connected systems
files: Connects to and indexes SaaS tools via read-only connectors.
value: Unified search across an organization's entire SaaS stack, with a knowledge assistant that answers from the real content rather than generic training data. Particularly valuable in organizations where institutional knowledge is fragmented across many tools.
engine: Proprietary retrieval models plus frontier LLMs for answer generation, grounded on company content.
latency: Search is near-instant. Generated answers take a few seconds.

pricing.includes: All connectors, AI assistant, admin controls

quality: Strong when the source content is well-maintained. As with all RAG systems, the answers are only as current as the indexed content.
tagline: Enterprise search that connects every SaaS tool and answers from your own content.
use_cases: Finding anything across Slack, email, Confluence, Jira, Drive, and 100+ other sources
Answering questions from internal documentation without knowing where it lives
Reducing time spent finding information as a recurring daily tax
governance_note: The information-disclosure risk from Glean runs in the same direction as with Microsoft Copilot and Notion AI: it surfaces content the user already has permission to see, but it surfaces it faster and in response to natural language questions. If permission settings are permissive, previously obscure content becomes easily discoverable. Run a permission audit on the connected sources before deploying rather than after discovering that an AI answered a question with a confidential document the user technically had access to.
training_optout: Glean does not train its models on customer content. The data stays indexed in a dedicated tenant. Verify the current DPA.
